title: Linux Shell Pseudo Device Reverse Shell
author: Raven Tait, Splunk
description:
The following analytic detects the use of shell's /dev/tcp or /dev/udp pseudo-device feature to establish outbound network connections.
This special file system interface allows opening a network socket and sending or receiving data using simple shell commands.
Attackers commonly abuse this native shell capability to create reverse shells without requiring external tools such as netcat, by redirecting shell I/O over a TCP or UDP connection to an attacker-controlled host and port.
